body.text: In short:
A jury has been shown CCTV of Beau Lamarre-Condon buying a surfboard bag days before he allegedly shot Sydney couple Jesse Baird and Luke Davies.
Prosecutors allege Mr Lamarre-Condon planned to use it to dispose of Mr Baird's body, who was his ex at the time.
He has pleaded not guilty to two counts of murder and one of aggravated break and enter.

A jury has been shown footage of former Sydney police officer Beau Lamarre-Condon buying a surfboard bag prior to the alleged murders of Jesse Baird and Luke Davies, which prosecutors allege he planned to use to dispose of Mr Baird's body.
Mr Lamarre-Condon has pleaded not guilty to two counts of murder and one of aggravated break and enter, with a NSW Supreme Court trial in its first week.
The 31-year-old is accused of shooting Mr Baird and his new boyfriend, Luke Davies, with his police pistol at Mr Baird's share house in Paddington, in Sydney's east, in February 2024.
The Crown alleges he formed an obsessive and jealous infatuation with Mr Baird, who had twice broken things off with him and requested no further contact.

Mr Lamarre-Condon's defence counsel has flagged with jurors that self-defence will be argued, and that it is his case that Mr Baird and Mr Davies died during two separate struggles in the Brown Street property, both involving his service pistol.
Surfboard bag

During the Crown's opening address, jurors were told Mr Lamarre-Condon was accused of planning Mr Baird's alleged murder in February 2024, including by stopping at a sports store days before to buy a surfboard bag to dispose of his body.
A friend was with Mr Lamarre-Condon at the time, the court was told.
On Thursday, the jury was played CCTV of inside a store on February 17, 2024, showing Mr Lamarre-Condon and the friend looking at surfboard bags.
In the footage, he held up a bag next to the friend.

Crown Prosecutor Brett Hatfield SC previously told the jury he anticipated evidence from the friend that the accused asked him whether he would fit inside the surfboard bag, to which the friend replied "probably not".
Mr Hatfield said it would be the friend's evidence that the accused then said: "I'll grab this one instead, it should be big enough."

The footage played today was among several compilations of CCTV footage being shown, including footage of Mr Lamarre-Condon arriving and leaving Balmain Police Station the previous day, driving his Tesla, and stopping at ATMs.
The jury was also shown footage of Mr Baird and Mr Davies at the Beresford in Surry Hills on the afternoon of February 18, 2024.

CCTV footage from the following day, when the alleged murders occurred, showed Mr Lamarre-Condon driving to Mr Baird's suburb, where prosecutors said he waited for hours near the home for two housemates to leave.
In one clip, he stood on the street dressed as an Uber Eats delivery driver, including high-visibility clothing and a helmet, while carrying a paper delivery bag.

Security camera footage from a neighbour's property recorded audio of three gunshots that morning, which the Crown had previously said occurred at 9:49am, another gunshot four seconds later, and then another 51 seconds later.

The officer in charge of the investigation, Detective Sasha Pinazza, told the court investigators obtained thousands of hours of footage from 200 or more locations, covering the period of February 16 to February 23, 2024.
Prosecutors have told the jury that Mr Lamarre-Condon allegedly murdered Mr Davies to eliminate him as a witness to the alleged murder of Mr Baird.

The Crown said after the alleged shootings, the accused bought a second surfboard bag, in addition to allegedly cleaning the scene and using a hire van to transport the men's bodies, which were ultimately found at a rural area south of Sydney.
Social media posts
The jury had previously heard that in mid-November 2023, Mr Baird confronted the accused about his use of social media to post photographs which gave the impression they were together.
This included an Instagram story showing a bouquet of flowers and captioned: "When he's in Melbourne but still sends you these."
The Crown says Mr Lamarre-Condon targeted the audience of these Instagram stories to include people he believed were his romantic rivals, but restricted Mr Baird from seeing them.
The jurors have been read a message from Mr Baird which requested no further contact and described his behaviour as "completely inappropriate".

They were also read a message from Mr Lamarre-Condon from November 18, 2023, in which he called Mr Baird a "manipulative player" and said "you pull at people's heart strings and expect no repercussions".
Mr Lamarre-Condon's childhood friend takes the witness box
This afternoon, a childhood friend of Mr Lamarre-Condon told the court he contacted her and said he needed to "ask something quickly" on November 23, 2023.
The friend, known as the pseudonym Alex Carrol during the proceedings, testified that on a FaceTime call, Mr Lamarre-Condon asked whether her ex-partner could get him a gun.
She said he mouthed the words, but she could understand what he was saying, and told the court he made a gun gesture with his hand at the time.
Ms Carrol said when she laughed and questioned why he would need one, Mr Lamarre-Condon "kind of shrugged it off" and the call ended quickly afterwards.
Under cross-examination by John Stratton SC, Ms Carrol disagreed that the defendant instead asked if her ex-partner had a gun, "in the context of being concerned about your safety".
The trial, before Justice Natalie Adams, has an estimated duration of three months.
